items.note: The original recipe called for two 4.5 oz jars of strained carrots (9 oz total). The modern equivalent is jarred baby food carrot puree, which is now commonly sold in 4 oz jars. You will need 9 oz total, so buy three 4 oz jars and weigh out the correct amount, or make your own fresh carrot puree.
The original recipe did not specify the oil used. It is assumed any neutral cooking oil will work.
Drain excess liquid from the pineapple.
The original recipe did not specify what type of nut, but walnuts or pecans will work best.

instructions.content: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a medium mixing bowl, mix Flour, Sugar, Baking Soda, Cinnamon, and Salt.
Whisk in Carrot Puree, Vegetable Oil, Eggs, and Vanilla Extract.
Fold in the Crushed Pineapple, and if using, the Shredded Coconut and Chopped Nuts.
Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 30-35 minutes.
In a small bowl, beat Cream Cheese, Margarine, Vanilla Extract, and Powdered Sugar until smooth.
When done, remove the cake from the oven and cool to room temperature.
notes: Doneness can be checked by inserting a toothpick near the center of the cake. The cake is not done if wet batter sticks to the toothpick.

instructions.content: Once cooled to room temperature, chill in the refrigerator for 30-60 minutes.
notes: Chilling before icing the cake can prevent tearing the cake.

instructions.content: Once chilled, frost the cake and serve.
notes: It is recommended to divide the cake with three cuts along the long edge, and five along the short edge.
